summary.final_text:
The Bradford assay ran and the plate was read at 595 nm. Well A1 gave an absorbance of **0.3155**. The other wells read about 0.04–0.06.

What I did:
1. Took 10 µL of the unknown protein sample from `reagents:A4` and dispensed it into `assay_plate:A1` (tip `tips:A1`, dropped afterward).
2. Took 200 µL of Bradford dye reagent from `reagents:A3` and dispensed it into `assay_plate:A1` (fresh tip `tips:A2`, dropped afterward).
3. Read `assay_plate` at 595 nm.

I can't convert the 0.3155 reading to a protein concentration. The plate has no BSA standard curve, and I didn't run any replicate wells. To get a concentration, the next step is to run BSA standards (from `reagents:A2`) on the same plate and fit a curve. I can set that up if you want.

task_def.source: Bradford microplate procedure as in Bio-Rad Bulletin 2674: 10 uL of sample plus 200 uL of diluted dye reagent per well, absorbance read at 595 nm.
task_def.prompt: Run a Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample: in assay_plate well A1, combine 10 uL of the sample with 200 uL of Bradford dye reagent, then read the plate at 595 nm.
